## Exact vs. Fuzzy Matches — What's the Difference?

| | How it was retrieved | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Stat cards (0–3 and 4–7)** | Opened by exact canonical ref (`open_entity`). Every HP, Move, Attack, immunity, and note value comes directly from the structured record. | **Exact — treat as authoritative** |
| **Ability card (Music Note2 Solo)** | Also opened by exact canonical ref. Initiative and abilities are confirmed from the record's own fields. | **Exact — treat as authoritative** |
| **Scenario cards** (Bandit Camp #1, Black Barrow #7, A Friend in Need #66, Wild Melee #84, Caravan Escort #91, A Night Out #85, Battle of the Bards #97) | Returned by `search_knowledge` as **fuzzy semantic matches**. The snippets confirm Bandit Scout appears in those scenarios' monster lists, but the scenario records themselves were **not opened**. Room layouts, special rules, and full monster deployment details from those scenarios are unverified in this run. | **Fuzzy — summaries only; open individually to confirm details** |

**Bottom line:** For the stat cards and the solo ability card, you have fully verified, field-level data. For the scenario references, you have reliable name-and-monster-list snippets but no opened record detail — look up any individual scenario before relying on its specifics at the table.
